title: Dave Canales: 'The Lights Will Never Be Too Bright for Those Two'
headline: Panthers beat Lions on SNF; Bryce Young-Tetairoa McMillan connection hit after a rough practice week, Chuba Hubbard ran with violence, and Monroe Freeling and Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) left injured ahead of the Week 5 bye.
summary: Canales praised the blackout crowd for forcing Detroit false starts and energizing the defense late in a Sunday night win. He said RPOs gave the offense balance, loosening the defense and letting Carolina dictate zone or man; when Detroit went to man, they hit a deep touchdown to Tetairoa McMillan, and Darren Waller got open a couple of times. He admitted it was a poor practice week for Bryce Young and McMillan, with near misses, but they kept working and connected under the lights. Chuba Hubbard was praised for breaking tackles and running with violence as the run game got going, helped by play action. The defense held Detroit to field goals in the red zone, and Canales called it their best defensive practice week, singling out Nick Scott's return for directing traffic. Corey Bullock stepped in after a first-series sack and the line settled down, with little interior pressure afterward. On injuries, Monroe Freeling could not finish the game and will be evaluated, while Jaelan Phillips appears to have a hamstring injury of unknown severity. The Week 5 bye comes at a good time with many players trying to return from injury, and Canales said he'll challenge the team on special teams penalties and discipline.

injuries.detail: Could not finish the game; full evaluation to come, no details yet.
Looks like a hamstring injury right now; severity unknown and he couldn't return to the game.

signals.claim: McMillan will continue to be a featured downfield target in the passing game, including deep shots against man coverage.
signals.note: He caught a huge deep touchdown, and the connection with Young appears to be improving after a rough practice week.
Young and McMillan worked through practice misses and delivered in the game, and the RPO balance helped the passing offense.
signals.quote: the lights will never be too bright for those two

signals.claim: Hubbard remains the lead back, fueling the run game with tackle-breaking and physical running.
signals.note: Canales praised his attitude and tackle-breaking as the run game got going, a good sign for his volume and efficiency.
signals.quote: what I loved about Chuba tonight was breaking tackles.

signals.claim: Waller will keep getting open in the passing game.
signals.note: Canales highlighted him running away from coverage a couple of times as part of the offensive balance.
signals.quote: Darren Waller running away a couple of times.

signals.claim: Phillips may miss time with a hamstring injury, severity to be determined.
signals.note: The bye week gives him extra recovery time, but his availability for Week 6 is uncertain.
signals.quote: Jaylen looks like a hamstring right now. We don't know the severity of that.

signals.claim: Freeling will undergo a full evaluation after leaving the game.
signals.note: An injury to a starting offensive lineman could affect the run game and pass protection; the bye gives some time.
signals.quote: he, he could not finish the game. We'll do a full evaluation on it

signals.claim: Bullock stepped in on the offensive line after the first-series sack and the line settled down.
signals.note: He may keep a larger role if Freeling's injury lingers.
signals.quote: I'm so glad Corey was able to step in for us today.

signals.claim: Scott is back in the defensive secondary and directing communication.
signals.note: His return stabilizes the defense, which had its best practice week and held Detroit to field goals.
signals.quote: It's great to have Nick back out there.

topics.detail: RPOs played off the run game to give the offense optionality and dictate coverage to the defense, while play action also helped the run game.

Carolina's red zone defense held Detroit to field goals. Canales called it the team's best defensive practice week and praised the pass rush discipline, with batted passes and little interior pressure.
The Week 5 bye lets the team heal injured players and review the first quarter of the season to see what works. Canales also plans to address special teams penalties and discipline.

title: Ben Johnson pleased with defense’s performance vs. Jets | Press Conference
headline: Tyson Bagent starts again with Caleb Williams out week-to-week, Kyle Monangai's thumb is day-to-day, and Roschon Johnson may get a bigger red-zone role as D'Andre Swift's role stays open ahead of the Packers.
summary: Ben Johnson was happy with the 3-1 start and the defense's effort against the Jets, but said execution still needs work in all three phases. He said Tyson Bagent ran a smooth, clean operation in his first start. Johnson wants him to protect the ball better, including on the interception that was negated, without losing his aggressiveness, since he missed some chances for big plays downfield. Caleb Williams is rehabbing well but won't play this week and is week-to-week. Kyle Monangai's thumb is expected to be okay, though he is day-to-day. Johnson called the red zone problems different each week, mostly details and installation this week, and said Roschon Johnson's bigger frame could help near the goal line because of Swift's red-zone struggles. He gave no commitment on Swift's role after the fumble, saying roles are set during the week of practice. He praised Dayo Odeyingbo's high-effort interior rush and Theo Benedet's improved run blocking at left tackle. He also credited the defense, led by DA's coverage mixes, for affecting the quarterback and handling two sudden-change situations.

injuries.detail: Won't be available this week; Johnson called it a week-to-week situation and said his rehab is going well.
Thumb injury. Johnson thinks he'll be okay but called it day-to-day, and his status will be clearer as the week goes on.

signals.claim: Bagent will keep starting at QB while Caleb Williams is out this week.
signals.note: Bagent is the starting QB for the Packers game, with the offense saying its playbook doesn't change much by QB.
signals.quote: pleased with where he was at for the first week

signals.claim: Williams will not play this week and is considered week-to-week.
signals.note: He is not an option for the Packers game and his return timeline is open-ended.
signals.quote: he's not going to be there this week for us

signals.claim: Monangai's thumb injury is day-to-day and his availability will be clearer through the week.
signals.note: Monitor his practice participation before locking him into lineups.
signals.quote: more of a day to day type deal

signals.claim: Roschon Johnson could get more red-zone or goal-line work because of his bigger body.
signals.note: He could take short-yardage and goal-line carries from Swift and Monangai, which would boost his touchdown equity.
signals.quote: he might be part of the solution as well

signals.claim: Swift's role this week is not guaranteed to match last week's and will be decided in practice.
signals.note: After his fumble and red-zone issues, his workload and goal-line share are uncertain.
signals.quote: each role is determined through the week of practice

signals.claim: Odeyingbo will keep a significant role as an interior pass rusher.
signals.note: He has been productive in all four games, which is useful for IDP managers.
signals.quote: playing at a really high level

signals.claim: Benedet is playing left tackle next to Joe Thuney and is expected to keep growing in that spot.
signals.note: A more stable left side helps the run game and QB protection.
signals.quote: it's a good start for him

topics.detail: Johnson said the issues vary by week: negative plays like penalties and negative runs the previous week, and sloppy details this week. He wants better installation and a strong Friday red-zone practice.

Johnson praised the defense's poise on two sudden changes, which held the Jets to two field goals. He credited tighter rush integrity, smaller coverage windows and DA's coverage mixing, and said it needs to get tighter against the run.

Johnson wants Bagent to protect the ball without losing aggressiveness. He said the negated interception over the middle was a decision Bagent has to make better. He also wants Bagent to improve his ball location and take more shots downfield.
Johnson called the kickoff return unit's performance not very good and an area for improvement.
Johnson called it a big week for the organization and said nothing new about the rivalry compared with last year.

title: HC Sean Payton on deciding Week 4 plays: 'Those guys made ‘em'
headline: Denver's offense is stuck in neutral against soft-shell defenses; RJ Harvey is the underneath outlet, Courtland Sutton is a concern, and Pat Bryant and two corners got hurt.
summary: Payton called the Week 4 loss to the 49ers a tight game decided by a couple of plays that San Francisco made and Denver didn't. The offense managed only about 30-some yards at halftime. He said it has to improve and that the team will look at everything on film, but he declined to discuss the play-calling question, calling it too early. He blamed the defense's late slide on time of possession and a big special-teams turnover (a fumble upheld on replay) that flipped the field. Injuries hurt the defense: both corners were down entering the second half, which can limit dime packages, and receiver Pat Bryant also got hurt. Payton said the receiver room has enough depth that Bryant's exit didn't change the plan. He chose a field goal on fourth-and-2 early in the fourth quarter because points felt at a premium. He said the 49ers' soft, deep shells made second and third downs tough, and that false starts need cleaning up. He admitted the Sutton usage is not clicking and said Denver has to fix it fast heading into Week 5.

injuries.detail: Left the game hurt after a 30-yard play. Payton had no update, said he is a good starter, and said the offense has other receivers.

signals.claim: Denver will look for ways to get Sutton more involved, including moving him off the outside, after a quiet game.
signals.note: Sutton's usage is a stated problem. His volume could rise with schematic tweaks, but nothing is fixed yet.
signals.quote: we got to figure it out fast because. you know, we're going into week five

signals.claim: Harvey will keep getting underneath targets when defenses play soft coverage.
signals.note: Harvey produced a big receiving game against soft coverage. That underneath role looks sticky if opponents keep dropping deep.
signals.quote: there were some big plays, you know, made by him.

signals.claim: Bryant's injury did not change the offense's plan, and others will absorb his snaps if he is out.
signals.note: Bryant's status is unknown. If he misses time, the other receivers get a bump.
signals.quote: he's a good starter. I mean a good player for us.

topics.detail: Denver had about 30-some yards at halftime and often faced long downs. Payton pointed to the 49ers' soft shell, inefficiency on second down, and early false starts. He said the offense needs better efficiency and answers against defenses that stay high and deep.
Asked about the play-calling situation, Payton said it is too early to discuss. He said the staff reviews everything each week.

Both corners were down entering the second half, which hurts dime packages. Payton said nickel is still possible because a player can play inside. He said the defense played well for a long stretch before time of possession and the special-teams turnover wore it down.
Payton considered going for it on fourth-and-2 from the 22 early in the fourth quarter but took the points because the game felt tight. A later two-point chance came up.
Denver's sideline had a poor angle on the fumble. The officials told Payton only that replay review ruled it a fumble.
San Francisco rotated its coverage shells and stayed on top of deeper throws, so Denver's chances came underneath. Payton said Denver added run pressures in the second half to shift the front.

title: Campbell on Week 4 performance
headline: Lions fell to 2-2 after a loss to Carolina, and Campbell is not panicking but is open to changes. The offense needs a faster start and more efficiency, with Jameson Williams' double-move deep shots and Goff's downfield throws the only offensive notes.
summary: Campbell credited Carolina for laying it on the line and said Detroit dug itself a hole early, with penalties at critical moments hurting. The Lions had the ball with about two minutes left to win the game and could not finish, though he sees that chance as a silver lining. He said the defense was not good enough in coverage, was beaten early by quick RPOs, then gave up too many rushing yards in the second half, and produced no takeaways. He declined to discuss a defensive coordinator change or the personnel in the secondary, saying he'll work with what he has and mix in new schematic looks the team hasn't used much. He also said the offense must be more efficient, stop stalling out, and start faster. He took 100% responsibility for the discipline and penalty problems. He said he'll always do what is right for the team, without ruling out a move, and added that it's too early to panic at 2-2 with 13 games left. On the final drive, a double move with Jameson Williams was rolled over by the safety, the ball was held, and Goff was sacked. Goff was praised for stepping up and making big throws.

signals.claim: Williams will continue to be used on double moves and deep shots downfield.
signals.note: He is the intended deep target on the key late-game play, which supports his big-play upside, though it did not connect.
signals.quote: we had a double move on with, um, you know, with Jmo

signals.note: Campbell praised Goff's downfield throws, a positive sign for the passing offense despite the loss and slow start.

topics.detail: Campbell said the coverage was not good enough, RPOs hurt early, the run defense slipped in the second half, and there were no takeaways. He said the defense has allowed over 31 points per game and wants to mix in new schemes and coverage/pressure combinations.
Penalties at critical moments hurt. Campbell said the problem is 100% on him and that he will get it fixed.
Campbell said the offense must be more efficient, avoid stalling out, and get a faster start, after being down two scores and fighting back.
Carolina's Bryce Young was praised for his quick release, mobility and processing, and McMillan had 14 catches for 92 yards and two TDs, helped by Coker's injury.
Campbell declined to discuss a defensive coordinator change and said he will always do what is right for the team. He said it is not time to panic at 2-2.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Tank Dell, Defensive Fixes & Titans Week | Full Q&A
headline: Tank Dell, Braden Smith and Kayden McDonald get their 21-day practice windows opened this week, while Kenneth Murray's concussion and Brevin Jordan's return are the other notable personnel items for Houston at 0-4.
summary: Ryans said Houston is 0-4 after another close loss to Dallas. He pointed to a lack of complementary football: special teams and defense gave up explosives and a touchdown, and the offense had too many three-and-outs. He repeatedly blamed defensive technique and communication breakdowns, saying CeeDee Lamb was moved all over the formation and made a lot of plays. He gave a noncommittal "We'll see how all that goes" when asked about taking back defensive play calling. He also said he would look at everything to see how he can help the defense. On offense he praised the game plan from Coach Kelly, with first-down shots, motion at the snap and C.J. Stroud playing well. He singled out Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson for big plays, and said the run game needs better finishing blocks up front. Tank Dell, Braden Smith and Kayden McDonald will have their practice windows opened, but their availability for Sunday depends on how they respond in practice. Kenneth Murray served as the green-dot defender and played well before leaving with a concussion. Brevin Jordan returned after two years and made an explosive play. Ryans also criticized penalties, including false starts and holding. Houston faces the Titans next.

topics.detail: Ryans said special teams, offense and defense all contributed miscues. A second-half special teams explosive and a defensive touchdown were examples, along with too many three-and-outs on offense.

Ryans blamed technique, dropped coverage and communication lapses. He said he will look at everything to see how he can help, and left open the possibility of taking back play calling by saying "We'll see how all that goes."
Dallas moved Lamb around to the slot, the outside and motion, which forced many different Houston defenders to cover him. Ryans credited Lamb as an outstanding player.
Ryans said the line needs to finish blocks better and strain harder to improve the run game.

Coach Kelly's game plan emphasized winning first down and taking shots, using motion at the snap on a high percentage of plays. The first play of the game was a big explosive to C.J. Stroud's target over the middle.
Ryans said some aggressive penalties, such as the Kamari Lassiter illegal contact, are bang-bang. He called false starts, holding and the penalties on kick return unacceptable and controllable.
Houston is 0-4, with three of those losses close. Ryans stayed optimistic and focused on the Titans without worrying about historical playoff odds.

title: Andy Reid: '[It Was a] Hard-Fought Battle Against a Good Football Team' | Postgame Press Conference - NFL Week 4
headline: Tyquan Thornton left with an ankle injury that 'doesn't look good' and Rashee Rice tweaked a hamstring. Kenneth Walker III is producing and Reid says he should get more carries. Xavier Worthy is also playing well.
summary: Reid called the win over the Raiders a hard-fought battle against a good team. The main costs were injuries at receiver: Tyquan Thornton's ankle looks bad and he will be evaluated further after flying back with the team, and Rashee Rice tweaked a hamstring. Reid praised the other receivers for stepping up as 'next man up.' Kenneth Walker III had another big day, including a 76-yard run with three tight ends on the field. Reid admitted he should have called more runs for Walker, who averaged 8.8 yards per carry. He said he is comfortable giving Walker the ball on any down. Reid said Xavier Worthy had a big day and could have had more catches if pressure hadn't prevented some throws. He also said the offense hit four deep passes against man, zero and blitz looks. Reid declined to discuss Kingsley Suamataia, calling it a disciplinary matter between the two of them rather than a performance issue. He praised the defense for holding Las Vegas to 72 rushing yards, and called special teams the best of the three phases. The team now has a bye week before facing the Chargers.

injuries.detail: Ankle injury that Reid said 'doesn't look good.' He flew back with the team and will get further evaluation.
Tweaked his hamstring during the game. No further timeline given.

signals.note: Reid admitted he should have fed Walker more and trusts him in all situations, which supports a high-volume role.

signals.note: He is a big-play option, and his role may grow if Thornton and Rice are limited.
signals.quote: he's playing good football.

signals.note: He had a strong game and season, but the injury puts his availability in doubt. Receiver targets could shift.

signals.quote: I do trust him to, uh, that he's going to do the right thing

signals.quote: That's between Kingsley and I.

topics.detail: Reid said he leaned on play-action and passing early because the run game wasn't gaining as much yardage, then admitted he should have run more once Walker was producing. The 76-yard run came from a three-tight-end set.
The defense held the Raiders to 72 rushing yards under Spagnuolo's game plan and came up with a late interception. A corner had ten tackles.

Reid called special teams the best phase, citing a fake punt, good returns from Remigio, and a forced fumble on a kickoff that he named the play of the game. Emmett Johnson is also working as a returner for the first time in his career, and Reid praised his instincts.
Reid said Kubiak has the Raiders playing disciplined football with few turnovers or penalties, and that the rivalry is healthy when both teams are good.
The Chiefs have a bye week next and then face the Chargers. Reid stressed handling the bye well.

title: Sean McVay, Byron Young & Kobie Turner discuss the Rams' Week 4 win over the Eagles, riding momentum into Monday Night Football & more
headline: Puka Nacua came out of the Eagles win healthy after a 100+ yard game and a rushing TD. Aaron Donald is hoped to play vs. Buffalo, Jaylen Watson is trending toward playing, and Myles Garrett's return window opens after the Bills game.
summary: McVay said the Rams' first three quarters in Philadelphia were marred by poor execution, inconsistent run blocking and too many penalties. He said the team woke up in the fourth quarter, when two long scoring drives (98 and 78 yards) won the game. Matthew Stafford went about 12-of-15 on the last two drives, and McVay said the rain did affect some early throws. Puka Nacua was at his best late. He had a 30+ yard third-down catch, another 100+ yard game, a rushing touchdown and a lead block on a Kyren Williams goal-line TD, and he came out feeling healthy with no pitch count. Terrance Ferguson went on IR with a medial ankle sprain and will miss at least four games, though McVay expects him back this season. McVay hopes Aaron Donald can practice and play this week, and he will give an update on Myles Garrett's possible return on Thursday. He expects Jaylen Watson to be ready for the Bills if he feels good in practice. Emmanuel Forbes had only a knee contusion, and another player left with a shoulder (rotator cuff) contusion but is expected to be okay. McVay called the defense excellent, citing pressure, a 1-of-14 mark on conversion downs and one fourth-down conversion allowed, with Byron Young standing out late. Special teams was called not good enough, though Alex Bachman fielded cleanly in his first game as returner.

topics.detail: McVay was frustrated by pre-snap procedural penalties and said the coaches need to emphasize them more. Staff members also drew criticism for interacting with Eagles fans, and he said it won't happen again.
A missed field goal and a long punt return allowed were called not good enough. The return game needs better perimeter blocking and the coverage unit needs to tackle better.
Philadelphia converted 1 of 14 third/fourth-down chances and was held out of the end zone in the second half. A fourth-down tush push stop was a turning point.
Rain affected some early Stafford throws and the exchange, but McVay said Stafford wouldn't use it as an excuse.
McVay praised Josh Allen, Joe Brady's offense, James Cook, Dalton Kincaid, Khalil Shakir and Dawson Knox, and said the Rams must play cleaner football for all three phases.

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Seahawks
headline: Harbaugh defended a three-man RB rotation (Omarion Hampton's carries have dropped since Week 2), praised Herbert despite 6 INTs and heavy hits, and gave no updates on Rashawn Slater or Joe Alt.
summary: Harbaugh spoke after a loss that dropped the Chargers to 1-3, per the 'four record' questions, and kept his message on fight, growth and staying the course. He said three running backs are playing well and rotating carries because that is best for the team, and he would not explain why the rotation began in Week 3 rather than earlier. He called Justin Herbert's performance one of the grittiest he has been associated with and said he respects no player he has coached more. He declined to say how comfortable Herbert looked in the first half. He said Herbert was supposed to read a linebacker who moved inside and then back outside on one interception, a point they covered at halftime. He admitted protecting Herbert is always at the front of his mind after the hits he took, but said he did not know Herbert's health status. He gave no updates on Rashawn Slater or Joe Alt. He praised four young offensive linemen who had to play at once: Jake Slaughter moved to guard, Logan Taylor went from guard to tackle, and Jacob Spomer and Travis Burke came in. He said offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job is not in jeopardy and that the team will not make significant changes, pointing to back-to-back fourth-quarter touchdown drives as a good sign.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Justin Herbert’s “Inspiring” Resilience
headline: Chargers' offensive line is badly depleted: Rashawn Slater has a high ankle sprain and may go to IR, Joe Alt has a neck injury, and Trevor Penning is in the concussion protocol. Herbert should keep playing behind a patchwork line.
summary: Harbaugh confirmed that a player the transcript calls "Sean" has a high ankle sprain. Context points to Rashawn Slater, who is still being evaluated and is more of an IR possibility than Joe Alt, whose neck injury is also being evaluated. Trevor Penning is in the concussion protocol and Donte Jackson has a hamstring issue. Harbaugh called losing Slater "significant" and gave no timeline. The line plan is "next man up" and a "one game season" approach. Four rookie linemen, plus Cole Strange and Jake Slaughter, played in the game and he was very pleased with them. He spent much of the session praising Justin Herbert's resilience and said Herbert moved on immediately after his first-half interception. He credited halftime adjustments on both offense and defense and the team's "complementary" second half, including a fourth-quarter stop on downs. On the three-way running back split he refused to explain the carry distribution, calling it game flow and personnel groupings, but said he likes how Omarion Hampton is playing and securing the ball. Dalvin Tomlinson, Charlie Kolar and Brenen Thompson are making progress, and the team expects to open the IR return window for Branson Taylor and Scott Matlock.

title: Klint Kubiak Postgame Presser - 10.4.26 | Week 4
headline: Jalen Nailor suffered a concussion; Raiders lost to KC, run game still searching, tight ends (Bowers, Mayer, Thomas) productive, Cousins praised.
summary: Kubiak opened by announcing that Jalen Nailor has a concussion. He said he was proud of the team's fight in a loss to the Chiefs, and he took responsibility for late-game problems: he did not get the final play in fast enough, and the call included a legal shift. He defended going aggressive on fourth down, including a penalty that took three points off the board, saying he regrets not converting rather than the decision itself. Asked about the run game, he admitted the team has to find answers and said there is 'more meat on that bone,' calling the backs and offensive line good. He also said the team has to go back to the drawing board against the run after Kansas City's backs got going. The offense gave the ball away too many times (minus two in turnover margin), and he said he'd need to watch the film on a fumble before commenting. He praised Kirk Cousins' play and leadership down the stretch ('that's why we brought him here') and called the tight end trio of Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas an impressive group that the team counts on every week. The team now turns to New England.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 5, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley's hamstring injury leaves his availability for the London game unresolved, with an update expected Wednesday. Sirianni also says the offense still lacks an identity and may move away from heavy shotgun use.
summary: Sirianni said Saquon Barkley hurt his hamstring and that the team will know more Wednesday, depending on how he responds to treatment. He did not rule Barkley in or out for Sunday. On offense, he said the team doesn't yet know its identity. The heavy shotgun usage isn't necessarily going to continue, and the team needs to be able to do multiple things. He admitted the offense failed on fourth-and-one and on third down at the two-yard line, and called goal-line and short-yardage execution a multi-cause problem that the staff is working through. Rookie tackle Markel Bell, who came in on short notice, was called solid. He got good movement on double teams and at the second level, though his game wasn't perfect. Sirianni said he is pleased with the left guard's play (apparently Cam, likely Cam Jurgens, who is not on the roster provided) and signaled no change. He declined to say who makes protection calls, but admitted protection was inconsistent, particularly against some blitzes. He gave no update on Lane Johnson. He said DeVonta Smith did not play and Dallas Goedert has been out, but used the injuries as no excuse. He also explained that the team will leave for London on Friday after a full week of practice.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald On The 30-23 Win vs. Chargers
headline: Seahawks are 3-1 and the run game is working, with Rashid Shaheed scoring from the backfield. Darnold and Emmanwori look healthy, Leonard Williams' ankle doesn't look serious, and Ty Okada has a shot to play this week.
summary: Macdonald said he is grateful for the 3-1 start but that the team is not yet playing to its own standard, citing ball security and penalties. He called the seven personal foul penalties unacceptable and said the next 24 to 48 hours will be spent addressing them directly. He praised the run game, naming Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, and said it was good to get Rashid Shaheed going, including his backfield touchdown on a Brian call. He said the defense stayed together to close the game, but run defense and end-of-half details need to improve. He highlighted linebacker play (back-to-back interceptions, Ernest Jones' tackle total) and said the staff has to find playing time for Drake Thomas, Nick Emmanwori, Nehemiah Pritchett and Trevon Diggs. He said Sam Darnold played tough behind too many hits and is fully ready to go. On health, Leonard Williams has an ankle issue that doesn't look serious, Emmanwori should be full go, and Ty Okada has a shot to play this week. He had no timeline for a player recently placed on injured reserve.

title: Kyle Shanahan Talks 49ers Win Over Broncos, Moves to 4-0
headline: 49ers are 4-0 with a run-heavy game plan. Deebo Samuel and George Kittle are fully producing, and Mike Evans played through rib pain. Kyle Juszczyk (knee sprain), Marques Sigle (ankle) and Upton Stout (shoulder) are the injury concerns going into Seattle.
summary: Shanahan said the physical game played out as the team expected. The plan was to run the ball a lot and stay balanced, and the defense made that possible by holding Denver down and keeping the ball coming back. A special teams turnover swung momentum after two three-and-outs to open the third quarter. He praised Dre Greenlaw, who was emotional against his former team, led the team in tackles and has had an outstanding season. He called Deebo Samuel huge as a runner and receiver, and said Kittle has looked unbelievable since Australia after the Achilles injury. Kittle's workload was managed early only because of conditioning, not because of any limit on his routes. Mike Evans played through significant rib pain and Shanahan tried to limit how many hits he took. Juszczyk's knee is thought to be a sprain with the ACL intact, Stout may have a shoulder AC injury, and Sigle left with an ankle injury, with more information due Monday. The offensive line has not allowed a sack in four straight games, and the team heads to Seattle next.
